AND {!$Input:Document.Email_Body__c} may also contain resume details so carefully get details from this as well

- projectName → Use the company/project name (e.g., "Consol Energy", "Zimmo"). - projectRole → Capture the specific role in the project (e.g., "Oracle PL/SQL Developer", "Consultant"). - designationJobTitle → Capture the official job title or designation given in the work experience (e.g., "Senior Software Engineer", "Business Analyst"). - clientName → Capture the client or organization for which the project was executed (e.g., "UTI Bank", "Renault Nissan"). If only an employer is mentioned, use that. - projectLocation → Capture the location if specified (e.g., "Chennai", "Bangalore", "Onsite – London"). - startDate / endDate → Extract from the timeline and normalize using ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).
- situation → Capture ONLY the high-level project context (industry, domain, project type, business objective, agile/phase info). - task → Capture ONLY the responsibilities and day-to-day duties (the “what was done”), e.g., requirement gathering, testing, document preparation, client meetings. - action → Capture ONLY the methods/approaches used (the “how it was done”), e.g., agile methodology, design standards, integrations, coding practices. - result → Capture ONLY the outcomes/achievements (the “what was achieved”), e.g., UAT sign-off, reduced defects, performance improvement, migration success. - responsibilities → Capture general responsibilities that are listed separately in the resume (if any). - achievements → Capture explicit "Achievements" or "Highlights" mentioned in the resume.
- learningOutcome → Candidate’s personal learning or takeaway (e.g., gained agile delivery experience, improved communication, new technical exposure). - skillsApplied → Capture the functional or technical skills actually applied during this project (e.g., PL/SQL, Data Modeling, BI Publisher). - toolsUsed → Capture tools/technologies explicitly mentioned (e.g., Oracle 12c, SQL Developer, Git, JIRA, Erwin). - environment → Capture the environment/platform stack if explicitly listed under "Environment" (e.g., Oracle 12c, SQL, Salesforce, SAP, AWS).
• Experience Extraction Rules - Extract only the candidate’s total years of professional experience. - Convert phrases like “2 decades” → "20 years". - Ignore software versions, product numbers, or unrelated numerics (e.g., "R12", "11i", "24/7"). - If multiple durations are mentioned, always select the largest value that clearly represents overall career span. - Output must be normalized as <number> years (e.g., "4 years", "10 years", "20 years"). - Do NOT copy descriptive sentences into this field. - If no valid years are found, leave it empty. • Email Handling Rule - If the email is already in correct format (<text>@<domain>.<tld>), keep it as-is. - If .com is missing, automatically append .com. Example: praveenkumbar16@gmail → praveenkumbar16@gmail.com. - If gmailcom or similar occurs (missing dot), insert the dot before the TLD. Example: praveenkumbar16@gmailcom → praveenkumbar16@gmail.com. - If the email ends with .co, .co.in, .org, .net, or other valid TLDs, keep as-is. Example: praveenkumbar16@gmail.co.in → praveenkumbar16@gmail.co.in. - If an email cannot be normalized into a valid format, leave it empty. - Never infer or generate an email if it is completely missing.
